title: Tenant Onboarding Role Crosswalk & SIEM Contract
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic crosswalk for tenant onboarding and RBAC v2 mapping across our three hosting modes (hosted, dedicated, private). It also defines the minimum SIEM export contract and an evidence-automation checklist for compliance audits.

Audience:
- Security engineers implementing tenant scoping and privilege boundaries
- SRE/Platform teams onboarding new tenants
- Solutions engineering doing enterprise onboarding

Scope / Non-scope:
- Scope: role-to-permission mappings by deployment mode; audit event schema requirements; evidence automation triggers and retention checkpoints.
- Non-scope: deep KMS/HSM configuration, network ACL designs, or provider billing flows.

High-level goals:
1) Reduce time-to-onboard for enterprise customers by providing a prescriptive role crosswalk and automation checklist.
2) Ensure SIEM receives consistent, tenant-scoped telemetry for access and evidence requests.
3) Provide a small set of policy templates to plug into onboarding workflows.

1) Tenant onboarding role crosswalk (RBAC v2)
Note: RBAC v2 introduces: tenant-scoped principals, resource-scoped roles, and activation windows for privileged roles.
Columns: RoleName | TypicalPersona | Hosted (boolean) | Dedicated (tenant-scoped) | Private (customer-managed) | Activation/Approval
- tenant-admin | Customer admin / SE | yes (logical tenant role) | yes (mapped to tenant project) | yes (mapped to local LDAP/AD) | 2FA + manager approval + audit ticket
- app-deployer | Platform engineer / CI | yes (API key with deploy scope) | yes (reserved GPU pool ops) | sometimes (depends on customer network) | CI token + deploy-audit event
- read-only-telemetry | SRE / CS | yes | yes | yes | auto (no manual approval)
- model-publisher | Solutions / ML Eng | yes (model register) | limited (by tenant policy) | depends | manager approval + signature for model provenance
- emergency-operator | Oncall SRE | yes (bounded) | yes (bounded) | no (customer-run) | require OTP + emergency ticket, 30m window

Guidance:
- Hosted: default roles exist in our control plane and are tenant-scoped by ID (tenant_id). No host-level keys grant cross-tenant access.
- Dedicated: map tenant roles to reserved project namespaces; operator roles include a ’dedicated-infra’ flag.
- Private: we provide policy templates and verification hooks; customers MAY map to their own IdP; we require delegation evidence for our runbooks to operate.

2) Minimal audit event schema (SIEM ingest contract)
We provide the minimum required fields every audit event exported to SIEM must include. The below is an example JSON blob that consumers should parse; it is included here as plain text for implementers.

EXAMPLE_AUDIT_EVENT (as string):
{
  "event_id": "uuid-v4",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-10T18:23:45Z",
  "tenant_id": "t-123456",
  "principal": {
    "id": "u-7890",
    "type": "user|service_account|api_key",
    "roles": ["tenant-admin"]
  },
  "action": "model.publish|deployment.create|iam.grant",
  "resource": {
    "type": "model|deployment|policy|key",
    "id": "m-3344"
  },
  "outcome": "success|failure|denied",
  "client_ip": "18.205.123.4",
  "user_agent": "redwood-cli/1.2.3",
  "request_id": "r-5555",
  "trace_id": "trace-abc",
  "details": "freeform-string-for-operator-info"
}

(Implementers: the audit emitter MUST stringify nested principal and resource fields; the top-level keys above must be present for every export.)

3) SIEM field mappings and contracts
- siem_index: redwood-audit-v1 (per-region partition)
- retention: default 365 days for hosted; configurable for dedicated; customer-defined for private (we require documentation of retention policy).
- required fields: event_id, timestamp, tenant_id, principal.id, action, outcome, request_id.
- optional fields that improve triage: client_ip, user_agent, trace_id, request_body_hash, response_status_code.
- sensitivity tagging: events that contain PII must be flagged with pii:true and redacted at source when possible.

Log shipping notes:
- Hosted: logs export via our secure forwarder (TLS + mTLS) to customer SIEM endpoints or to our managed SIEM integration.
- Dedicated: we push to tenant-managed collectors; we provide log forwarder container images and Helm charts.
- Private: we publish an export contract and helper scripts; customers host forwarder.

4) Evidence automation checklist (onboarding -> audit readiness)
- [ ] Tenant created in control plane with tenant_id assigned and metadata (legal entity, data residency)
- [ ] Roles provisioned from template (tenant-admin, app-deployer, read-only-telemetry)
- [ ] At least one RBAC policy bound to tenant-admin that is signed and stored as evidence artifact
- [ ] SIEM integration validated with sample event (use test_event_id)
- [ ] Automated evidence export job scheduled (daily) and verified for last 7 days
- [ ] Proof of 2FA enrollment for all users with tenant-admin role (screenshot or IdP assertion)
- [ ] Emergency operator activation drill executed and captured in audit logs
- [ ] Model provenance artifacts (hashes, sources) stored for any published model before external access

Automation triggers (recommended):
- On tenant creation: auto-provision default roles + push policy JSON to evidence-bucket (s3://redwood-evidence/tenant_id/YYYYMMDD/roles.json)
- On role grant: create Jira ticket (SEC-<tenantID>-grant) and link audit event to ticket ID in request_id
- On sensitive action (iam.grant, key.create, emergency.activate): immediate webhook to compliance-alerts channel + create evidence snapshot (policy, actor, timestamp)

5) Sample policy templates (plain snippets)
- Tenant admin (minimal):
  - allow: iam:read, iam:list, tenant:configure, billing:read
  - deny: infra:host-level-ops, server:shutdown
- App deployer (CI):
  - allow: deployment:create, deployment:update where deployment.tenant_id == ${tenant_id}
  - allow: image:pull from tenant registry

6) Edge cases and decision notes
- Cross-tenant support cases: Support engineers may be granted ephemeral cross-tenant bindings for triage. All such grants MUST be recorded as emergency-operator activation events with auto-expiry and manager approval.
- Dedicated operator keys: reserved for infra staff; always scoped to project and rotated on a 30d cycle.
- Private deployment telemetry: if customer refuses export, require signed attestation describing local retention and review cadence.

7) Implementation checklist for engineering teams
- SDKs: add tenant_id to all control plane clients and fail loudly if missing.
- Audit emitter: validate presence of required keys; provide test harness that asserts shape.
- Forwarder: ensure TLS + mTLS; document cert rotation.
- Evidence export job: implement incremental upload with atomic commit marker file.

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress):
- How granular should resource-level permissions be for model artifacts vs. model deployments? (Queued for design review - JIRA-SEC-4890)
- Retention SLA for Dedicated customers that purchase extended history; pricing and storage policy to be finalized.
- Decide canonical field for indicating redaction status (pii_redacted vs pii_masked).

Appendix: quick test procedure for onboarding validation
1) Create test tenant t-e2e-000, run onboarding script.
2) Verify roles.json exists in evidence-bucket and contains expected bindings.
3) Trigger a model.publish from customer test account and validate exported audit event in SIEM index redwood-audit-v1.
4) Execute emergency-operator activation: confirm one event with outcome=success and request_id linked to the created Jira ticket.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is meant to be prescriptive but lightweight; if you think a required field is missing from the audit schema, annotate inline and we will iterate.
- Implementation owners: Jared Nguyen (audit emitter), Lucia Romero (SIEM forwarder), Owen Blake (onboarding automation).

Unresolved: the team needs to align on a canonical evidence-bucket naming convention for private deployments; current proposal is s3://redwood-evidence/{deployment_mode}/{tenant_id}/ but may conflict with customer-run buckets.

End of doc.
